author: reek
body: Three of these are round-trips, and they are here because each one is a place where a silent error produces a picture that still looks like a reflection. A depth buffer that quantises, a normal that comes back unnormalised, a projection that disagrees with the ray it came from -- none of those announce themselves, they just make the reflection land in the wrong place, and no image will tell you which one did it.

author: reek
body: The projection has to be the exact inverse of the ray generator, or every reflection lands in the wrong pixel. Casting a ray through a known pixel and projecting a point on it back must return that pixel, offset by the half-pixel the ray generator aims through.

author: reek
body: The depth it returns is along the VIEW AXIS, not along the ray, so it equals the ray distance only down the centre of the screen and is shorter everywhere else by exactly the cosine between them. That is checked here rather than asserted: `want` is computed independently as `dist * dot(dir, forward)`.
